# AWS CloudFront

This plugin collects read-only metadata for the AWS CloudFront distributions in an account, evaluates CCF Rego policy bundles against each distribution, and emits evidence back through the CCF agent.

This page is for **operators** who run the `plugin-aws-cloudfront` plugin with the CCF Agent, and for **developers** who write policies for it. It documents [v0.1.2](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-aws-cloudfront/releases/tag/v0.1.2) and is generated from the plugin's [README at v0.1.2](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-aws-cloudfront/blob/v0.1.2/README.md).

## How it works

### How it fits in CCF

The CCF agent starts this binary through HashiCorp `go-plugin` (runner protocol v2), passes configuration and policy paths over gRPC, and receives generated evidence through the runner callback. This repository does not call the CCF API directly.

During `Init`, the plugin registers the `cloudfront-distribution` subject template (identified by `account_id` and `distribution_id`) and the subject and risk templates discovered from the supplied policy bundles.

## Configuration

| Key | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `policy_labels` | no | JSON object of extra labels added to every evidence, e.g. `{"team":"platform"}`. |

CloudFront is a global service, so there is no region setting: every AWS call (CloudFront and `sts:GetCallerIdentity`) goes to `us-east-1`. AWS credentials come from the default AWS SDK credential chain.

Any agent-supplied `policy_data` is passed through to Rego as `data.*`, on top of the bundle's own `data.json` (agent-supplied keys win).

## Evidence collected

### Data collected

For every distribution returned by the CloudFront `ListDistributions` API (all pages), the plugin reads its tags with `ListTagsForResource` and builds this policy input:

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `account_id` | the caller's AWS account |
| `distribution_id` | the distribution ID |
| `arn` | the distribution ARN |
| `domain_name` | the distribution's CloudFront domain name |
| `status` | the distribution status |
| `enabled` | whether the distribution is enabled |
| `certificate_arn` | the viewer certificate's ACM certificate ARN (omitted when there is none) |
| `cache_behaviours` | `path_pattern` and `viewer_protocol_policy` for the default cache behaviour (reported as path `/*`) and each path-based cache behaviour |
| `tags` | the distribution's tags (empty when they cannot be read) |

Each evidence carries the labels `provider=aws`, `type=cloudfront-distribution`, `distribution_id`, `resource_arn`, `account_id` and `domain_name`, plus any `policy_labels`.

## Policy input

One document per CloudFront distribution. CloudFront is global, so there is no region. The plugin builds the document from `ListDistributions` and `ListTagsForResource`, and a policy reads it as `input`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `account_id` | string | AWS account ID the plugin is running against. |
| `distribution_id` | string | ID of the distribution. |
| `arn` | string | ARN of the distribution. |
| `domain_name` | string | The distribution's CloudFront domain name. |
| `status` | string | Distribution status, `Deployed` or `InProgress`. |
| `enabled` | boolean | Whether the distribution is enabled. |
| `certificate_arn` | string | ARN of the ACM certificate the viewer connection uses. Omitted when the distribution uses no ACM certificate. |
| `cache_behaviours` | array of objects | The default cache behaviour first, with path pattern `/*`, then every other cache behaviour. Each has `path_pattern` (string) and `viewer_protocol_policy` (string: `allow-all`, `https-only` or `redirect-to-https`). |
| `tags` | object (string to string) | The distribution's tags. An empty object when it has none or when the tags could not be read. |

An example input:

```json
{
  "account_id": "111122223333",
  "distribution_id": "E2EXAMPLE1ABCD",
  "arn": "arn:aws:cloudfront::111122223333:distribution/E2EXAMPLE1ABCD",
  "domain_name": "d1example2abcd.cloudfront.net",
  "status": "Deployed",
  "enabled": true,
  "certificate_arn": "arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:111122223333:certificate/9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d",
  "cache_behaviours": [
    {
      "path_pattern": "/*",
      "viewer_protocol_policy": "redirect-to-https"
    },
    {
      "path_pattern": "/static/*",
      "viewer_protocol_policy": "https-only"
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "Environment": "production"
  }
}
```

## Subject templates

The subject templates this plugin registers. Each example is built from sample data.

### cloudfront-distribution

A CloudFront distribution. The plugin registers it as a component subject and attaches it to the evidence of every distribution it evaluates. Title: `CloudFront Distribution {{ .distribution_id }}`.

| Identity key | Description |
|---|---|
| `account_id` | AWS account ID. |
| `distribution_id` | CloudFront distribution ID. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "cloudfront-distribution",
  "type": "component",
  "title": "CloudFront Distribution E2EXAMPLE1ABCD",
  "description": "AWS CloudFront Distribution E2EXAMPLE1ABCD (d1example2abcd.cloudfront.net) in account 111122223333.",
  "purpose": "Represents an AWS CloudFront distribution evaluated for TLS compliance posture.",
  "identityLabels": {
    "account_id": "111122223333",
    "distribution_id": "E2EXAMPLE1ABCD"
  }
}
```

## Policies

The policy bundles that work with this plugin, at their newest releases. The controls are the ones the bundle's policies list in their metadata.

| Bundle | Latest version | Controls covered | Compatible plugin lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`plugin-aws-cloudfront-policies`](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-aws-cloudfront-policies) | `v0.1.1` | CC6.7 | latest |
